input.command:
python -c "
import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from lmfit.models import LorentzianModel,ConstantModel
d=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv');x=d.shift_cm1.values;y=d.intensity.values.copy()
y[np.argmax(y)]=np.nan
ok=~np.isnan(y)
for lo,hi,c in[(100,160,127),(280,340,306)]:
  m=ok&(x>lo)&(x<hi);mod=LorentzianModel()+ConstantModel()
  r=mod.fit(y[m],mod.make_params(center=c,amplitude=5e4,sigma=4,c=1500),x=x[m]);print(r.best_values,'fwhm',2*r.params['sigma'].value, r.params['center'].stderr)
for lo in range(60,1000,60):
  m=ok&(x>=lo)&(x<lo+60);print(lo,np.median(y[m]).round())
m=ok&(x>190)&(x<220);print(np.mean(y[m]),np.std(y[m]))
"

from lmfit.models import LorentzianModel,ConstantModel

y[np.argmax(y)]=np.nan

for lo,hi,c in[(100,160,127),(280,340,306)]:
  m=ok&(x>lo)&(x<hi);mod=LorentzianModel()+ConstantModel()

candidates.evidence: Two strong lines at 127.8 and 306.0 cm-1 match the A1'(1) (~134) and A1'(2) (~307-308) out-of-plane modes of GaSe. The 306 cm-1 line fits very well. The 128 line is about 6 cm-1 below the usual value. The commonly seen E' (~213) and E (~250) modes are not resolved.
The same family, but its modes are expected near 188, 295 and 360 cm-1, so it does not match.
Their strongest modes (Bi2Te3 ~102/134, InSe ~115/178/200/227, In2Se3 ~110/175/205) do not reproduce the 128 + 306 pair.

The E' (~213) and E (~250) modes are not detected, so the polytype (ε, β, γ) cannot be determined.
Layer number, strain and doping cannot be determined from this single unpolarized spectrum.
This is a single spectrum with no angle resolution, so no polarization-pattern classification is possible.
The 327 cm-1 point is a one-pixel spike and was excluded as a cosmic ray. The 204 cm-1 feature is within the noise.
The substrate is unspecified, and no Si 520.7 cm-1 line is visible.
